clue.text: She-goat that goes flying round the cathedral?

definitions.text: She-goat that goes flying round the cathedral?

parts.words: She-goat that goes flying round the cathedral?
parts.note: a goat is a butter (it butts), and its female form on the actor/actress pattern adds -ESS; a flying one is the masonry prop outside a cathedral

explanation.surface: A nanny goat careers round a cathedral close.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'She-goat' as a female butter (one that butts), made feminine like actress; 'goes flying' points to the flying kind of wall support seen on Gothic cathedrals.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying support of masonry propping a cathedral wall is the classic architectural prop named here, and the female-goat pun builds its spelling.

clue.text: Suited insect to cross river

clue.text: If this Athenian leaves an element, does any remain?

indicators.note: when the name departs from the element, what is left is the word any, so taking any out of the element gives the name

taken as written

explanation.surface: A philosopher wonders whether anything is left once an Athenian walks out of an element.
explanation.walkthrough: The question answers itself: remove the Athenian from ANTIMONY and ANY does remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon of Athens is the misanthropic Athenian of Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Free from ordeal, taking every other comfort

clue.text: Colonist keen to speak in former British possession

clue.text: Game made in one diamond?
